name: Deep Counter 5-4-1

slots.why: Keeps goalkeeping simple, then distributes quickly and directly toward the target man or wide outlets when a counter is available.
Defensive wing-back stays as part of the back five, protects the flank and only advances cautiously.
Defends the box simply as part of the back three. Cover is an alternative for a quicker, anticipatory defender, but only one centre-back should use Cover.

The central defender protects the middle of the box first. Ball-Playing Defender (Defend) is an alternative when one centre-back has enough passing, decisions and composure to launch counters reliably.
Defends the box simply as part of the back three. Cover is an alternative for a quicker, anticipatory defender, but only one centre-back should use Cover.
Defensive wing-back stays as part of the back five, protects the flank and only advances cautiously.
Winger (Attack) is the primary left-side counter-attacking outlet, using pace to carry the team upfield after deep regains.
Central Midfielder (Defend) holds the middle, protects the back five and keeps his positioning while the counter-attacking outlets break.
Central Midfielder (Support) connects deep regains to the target man and wide outlets and can join the second wave of the counter.
Winger (Attack) is the primary right-side counter-attacking outlet, using pace to carry the team upfield after deep regains.
Target Man (Support) provides the essential long outlet, competes for direct balls and holds possession long enough for the wingers and supporting midfielder to join.

description: A deep defensive 5-4-1 that protects the box with a back five and compact midfield, then escapes pressure through a strong target man and two fast wide counter-attacking outlets.
whyGood: It maximises defensive numbers without removing every attacking outlet. The target man gives direct clearances somewhere useful to go, while the two attacking wide midfielders provide enough pace and penetration to punish opponents who commit numbers forward.
whyThisShape: The back five and holding central midfielder prioritise the space around the box. The second central midfielder links rather than charging forward, while the two wide midfielders are deliberately more aggressive because they are the main counter-attacking runners. More direct passing, Pass Into Space and quick long goalkeeper distribution reduce the need to play through pressure. Regroup and a lower block preserve shape after losses. The central centre-back is a simple defender by default; BPD(D) is only worthwhile when a player has the distribution to turn deep regains into accurate counters.
whenToUse: When protecting a lead or playing away against a substantially stronger side, especially when you have a strong aerial striker and quick wide players who can turn clearances into genuine counters.
whenNotToUse: When you need sustained possession or must create a high volume of chances. Avoid it if the striker cannot secure direct balls or the wide players lack the pace to turn deep regains into territory.

instructionRationale.Lower Line of Engagement: Concedes harmless possession higher up the pitch and keeps the midfield close to the back five.
instructionRationale.Drop Off More Defensive Line: Removes space behind the defence and concentrates bodies around the box.
instructionRationale.Counter: Releases the wide outlets immediately after a regain rather than asking the whole team to build up.
instructionRationale.Pass Into Space: Targets the space left behind advancing opposition full-backs for the attacking wide midfielders.
instructionRationale.More Direct Passing: Uses the target man and wide outlets instead of asking a defensive side to play through pressure.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Restores the deep 5-4-1 structure immediately after possession is lost.
instructionRationale.Lower Tempo: Reduces unnecessary turnovers once the immediate counter is not available.
instructionRationale.Sometimes Time Wasting: Fits the tactic's main use cases without making every possession excessively passive.
instructionRationale.Less Urgent Pressing: Keeps players in the compact block rather than pulling them out to chase the ball.

keyRequirements: Three dependable centre-backs and defensive wing-backs capable of holding a compact deep block
Two genuinely quick wide midfielders who can turn deep regains into counter-attacks
A strong target man who can win or secure direct balls under pressure
A disciplined holding central midfielder and a reliable supporting connector
Enough concentration and positioning across the defensive unit to tolerate long periods without the ball
